gen_risks.description: Delay in passage of the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill could postpone the mandatory duty, leaving schools without a legal requirement to run free breakfast clubs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage early with legislative drafters, develop interim voluntary guidance for schools, and prepare a contingency rollout plan.
gen_risks.evidence: The Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools to offer a breakfast club.

gen_risks.description: Future years’ funding may not be secured, threatening programme continuity after year 1.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare a robust multi‑year business case, secure provisional budget commitments, and set aside a contingency reserve.
gen_risks.evidence: Funding for future years will be agreed separately through business cases.

gen_risks.description: The internal CRM system may not be ready by the November 2025 MVP deadline, hindering school onboarding and support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Allocate a dedicated development team, adopt agile milestones, and retain a manual onboarding fallback process.
gen_risks.evidence: Develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum‑viable product from November 2025.

gen_risks.description: The call‑centre pilot for data collection could fail to capture accurate attendance data, affecting funding calculations and monitoring.
gen_risks.mitigation: Pilot with clear KPIs, conduct early user testing, and retain school self‑reporting as a backup data source.
gen_risks.evidence: Start commercial processes to begin a call‑centre pilot to support data collection.

gen_risks.description: Cohort 1 schools may miss the April 2026 start date, compressing implementation timelines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set weekly progress checkpoints, provide early guidance packs, and allocate rapid‑response support for delayed schools.
gen_risks.evidence: Cohort 1 will begin delivery in April 2026.

gen_risks.description: A gap between the NSBP ending in July 2026 and FBC start in September 2026 could leave pupils without breakfast provision.
gen_risks.mitigation: Arrange interim bridging provision, communicate transition timelines early, and align procurement to ensure continuity.
gen_risks.evidence: NSBP will end in July 2026... invited to join the FBC programme, starting in September 2026.

gen_risks.description: Complexity of the funding model may cause confusion among schools, reducing uptake.
gen_risks.mitigation: Produce clear guidance, run webinars, and offer a dedicated help‑desk to answer funding queries.
gen_risks.evidence: Variation by disadvantage levels was deemed complicated; simplified model intended to be easier to understand.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient staffing for supervised childcare and food preparation could compromise club quality, especially in high‑disadvantage schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide recruitment incentives, leverage local‑authority staffing support, and allow flexible staffing ratios where appropriate.
gen_risks.evidence: Staffing levels are estimated and rounded... typical staffing patterns for mainstream, SEND and specialist settings.

gen_risks.description: Food supply chain disruptions may prevent schools from meeting required food standards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Qualify multiple approved suppliers, maintain buffer stock, and monitor market conditions continuously.
gen_risks.evidence: Food provided must be in line with school food standards.

gen_risks.description: Labour‑market inflation could outpace area cost adjustments, leading to under‑funded schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Review area adjustments annually and embed an inflation buffer within the funding formula.
gen_risks.evidence: Apply an area cost adjustment to the funding to account for variations in the labour market.

gen_risks.description: Persistently high pupil absence post‑pandemic may lower club take‑up, weakening the projected benefit‑cost ratio.
gen_risks.mitigation: Promote health‑safety measures, offer flexible attendance options, and monitor attendance trends to adjust outreach.
gen_risks.evidence: School absence significantly increased following the pandemic... still not returned to pre‑pandemic levels.

gen_risks.description: Advisers procured via the education and children’s social care framework may under‑perform, affecting school support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include strict performance clauses, conduct regular monitoring, and retain internal backup advisers.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement process to increase the number of advisers supporting schools through the educational and children's social care framework.

gen_risks.description: The independent evaluation may not deliver timely insights, limiting programme adjustments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set clear interim reporting milestones, appoint an evaluation steering committee, and ensure rapid dissemination of findings.
gen_risks.evidence: Evaluation will be independently commissioned and run from 2026 to 2028, with interim and final reporting.

gen_risks.description: A change in government priorities could reduce political support and resources for the programme.
gen_risks.mitigation: Embed the duty in legislation, build cross‑party advocacy, and showcase early success metrics.
gen_risks.evidence: The government has committed to create a new mandatory free breakfast club duty for all state‑funded schools.

gen_risks.description: Data‑privacy concerns around the CRM and call‑centre could lead to compliance breaches.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment, enforce GDPR‑compliant safeguards, and provide staff training.
gen_risks.evidence: Develop a customer relationship management system... schools engage with the department for 'first line' support.

gen_risks.description: Funding rates for special schools may be insufficient given higher per‑child costs, creating inequitable provision.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor special‑school cost data and adjust the per‑child rate if disparities emerge.
gen_risks.evidence: At special schools, the funding rate is: £1,000 start‑up grant, daily amount of £18.95, £3.23 for every child.

gen_risks.description: Governance processes may not flag emerging issues promptly, delaying corrective action.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce monthly project‑board reviews, define clear escalation paths, and assign dedicated risk owners.
gen_risks.evidence: Risks and issues are reviewed regularly, with challenges escalated as appropriate to the SRO and project directors through the monthly project board.

gen_risks.description: Area cost adjustments could over‑fund low‑cost regions, wasting taxpayer money.
gen_risks.mitigation: Periodically recalibrate adjustments against actual cost data and adjust allocations accordingly.
gen_risks.evidence: Apply an area cost adjustment to the funding to account for variations in the labour market.

gen_risks.description: Schools not meeting the 40% FSM threshold for Cohort 1 may feel excluded, harming stakeholder relations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Communicate transparent eligibility criteria and offer alternative support mechanisms for other schools.
gen_risks.evidence: Cohort 1... schools with 40% or more FSM 'Ever 6' pupils will be eligible to apply for a place.

gen_risks.description: If attainment benefits are lower than forecast, the benefit‑cost ratio could fall below 1, questioning value for money.
gen_risks.mitigation: Track early attainment outcomes, adjust programme scale, and implement cost‑efficiency measures as needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Sensitivity analysis halving attainment benefits still returns a positive BCR of 1.19.

gt_risks.description: Lower value for money compared to the 'do minimum' option in year 1, due to the shorter funding period available for the preferred option's new cohorts of schools.
Delivery risks around staffing and food costs for schools newly onboarded to the free breakfast clubs programme.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated through early adopter (EA) scheme insights and support funding.

gt_risks.description: Uncertainty in the labour-market benefits (parental workforce participation gains) the programme is expected to deliver.
gt_risks.mitigation: Addressed through conservative assumptions in the economic modelling.
